title: US, Israel Reportedly Plan Fresh Iran Strikes After Midterms; Tehran Threatens 'Father of All Bombs'
excerpt: A New York Times report carried by TOI and ANI says the two militaries have prepared a short, intensive campaign against Iran's energy, nuclear and missile sites, while an IRGC spokesperson promises an unspecified new weapon in response.
body:
• The United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, according to a New York Times report carried by The Times of India and by ANI — a short, intensive operation against Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities and missile and drone arsenal.
  • US War Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week to discuss renewed strikes, the report said; it remains uncertain whether President Donald Trump will approve a fresh operation.
  • Iran's IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi threatened to unveil a weapon Tehran calls the "Father of All Bombs," without giving any details of its capabilities.
  • A White House official said the administration does not comment on military plans "that may or may not exist," adding that Trump is keeping all options on the table to ensure Iran cannot acquire nuclear weapons.

The United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed military strikes on Iran after the American midterm elections, while Tehran has threatened to unveil a weapon it calls the "Father of All Bombs," according to reporting by The New York Times carried by The Times of India and in an ANI report published by Devdiscourse. Both accounts rest on the same New York Times reporting, citing US officials and others briefed on the deliberations — no US or Israeli government has confirmed the plans on the record.

What the Reported Plan Involves

The proposed operation would be short but intensive, targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities and its missile and drone arsenal. The two militaries have stepped up exercises, including flying aircraft over Iraq to practise strike manoeuvres, the report said. The United States is assembling a force expected to be fully in place by early November, including three aircraft carriers, thousands of Marines, fighter jets and Special Operations forces.

https://x.com/Truthtellerftm/status/2113124566159470903

Some US officials believe another round of attacks could push Iran's economy to the brink and force Tehran to make diplomatic concessions after nearly eight months of conflict. Washington is also seeking to use the threat of renewed action as leverage in negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme and control of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iranian negotiators have resisted concessions on the nuclear issue, insisting it be addressed later in the talks. The US and Israel reportedly came close to launching an attack earlier this month, but Trump postponed it shortly before it was due to begin. Israel's October 27 election could also affect timing, analysts said.

"The United States has the 'Mother of All Bombs.' We will show them the 'Father of All Bombs,' and it will definitely be something new for them."

— Hossein Mohebbi, IRGC spokesperson, via Iran's Student News Network

Tehran's Response

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iran was preparing to unveil the "Father of All Bombs," according to Iran's Student News Network (SNN), but provided no details about the weapon or its capabilities. He said Iran's missile stockpile had increased 1.5 times following the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025, and described a shift toward permanent deterrence and asymmetric warfare: if attacked, Iran would not only respond but go on the offensive.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian described the situation to Parliament as a "super-challenge, not a challenge," saying: "America didn't think we would stand firm despite the pressure and war, but we stood firm, and we will continue to stand firm." Mahdi Mohammadi, a senior adviser to Iran's negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, called the idea that the US could finish another round of strikes within 72 hours a "fantasy," saying Iran would determine when any war ends and warning that a renewed conflict could extend to data centres and underwater internet cables.

The 'Mother of All Bombs' Question

The Iranian threat follows reports that Trump has considered using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast — the "Mother of All Bombs," about 21,600 pounds and among the largest non-nuclear weapons in the US arsenal — against Iran's deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility. Weapons specialists have questioned whether a bomb that explodes above ground could destroy a site protected by granite layers, and military officials have raised concerns that it must be delivered by a slow MC-130 transport aircraft vulnerable to Iranian anti-aircraft fire.

What Happens Next

Trump's decision is the unresolved variable. Previous US-Israeli strikes between February and April drove up energy prices and inflation worldwide and strained the Pentagon's supply of missile interceptors, according to the report — a cost any new campaign would repeat. For now, the plans are reported, not announced, and both the strike threat and Tehran's "Father of All Bombs" claim remain unverified beyond the officials and state-affiliated outlets quoted above.
